Q55347059.summary: Only fragments remain of this silk banner, but a haloed figure in three-quarter view can still be made out, wearing a red stole over a robe that has faded almost to the colour of the silk, with small flowers scattered across the background. Crosses appear on his headdress, on a pendant at his chest and at the head of a staff, marking him as Christian although the pose and gestures recall Buddhist bodhisattva images. Found in the Library Cave at Dunhuang, it is a rare witness to the Church of the East in China and may represent Christ himself.
facts: The painting was recovered by Aurel Stein in 1908 from the Library Cave (Cave 17) of the Mogao Caves and is now in the British Museum.
The figure's red moustache and beard, rather than the green curling moustaches typical of bodhisattvas, are among the features that point to a Christian rather than Buddhist subject.
Scholars including Hans-Joachim Klimkeit and Christoph Baumer describe it as Christ or a saint, while others such as P. Y. Saeki and Tōru Haneda regarded it as an image of Christ.
